title: Innocence in the Crossfire: Roles of Skip Connections in Jailbreaking Visual Language Models
measurement_description: The paper evaluates the vulnerability of Visual Language Models (VLMs) to jailbreak attacks using toxic visual inputs. As part of this, the researchers include a dataset of harmful memes specifically targeting the Islamic community, measuring the Attack Success Rate (2-ASR) and analyzing the internal representations of the models across different layers to determine when the models distinguish between benign images and anti-Islam toxic memes.
findings: The paper found that Visual Language Models (VLMs) process toxic memes targeting the Islamic community differently from benign images, but this separation in internal representations occurs at different layers depending on the model (e.g., emerging around the 17th layer for LLaVA-V and immediately from the initial layer for MiniGPT4). Furthermore, harmful memes, including those targeting Muslims, proved to be just as effective as explicit toxic visuals in successfully jailbreaking the safety guardrails of the tested models.
